item.title: Understanding RoPE
item.description:
Need for Positional Encodings (PE)

A transformer language model[1] maps a sequence of vectors to a probability distribution over the next vector in the sequence. In language models, each of these vectors represent tokens. However, the tokens are invariant to their positions in the sequence. [add_citation?] and this is a problem because the order of tokens clearly matters for the next token prediction task.

This problem is solved with the introduction of positional Encodings (PE). A PE is a vector that contains information about the position of the token in the sequence. PE’s ideally should have the following properties :
